patient._comment: 'patient' contains the three sections that may be exposed in the detailed patient display: presentation, answer, and clinical.

presentation._comment: The immutable patient evidence package available for triage. Panel context controls whether other sections are locked or available.
presentation.chiefComplaint: Fever after returning from the Congo
presentation.quote: I got back from the DRC eight days ago. I was treating patients during the outbreak, and one shift my glove tore while I was cleaning up vomit. Yesterday the fever and body aches started; today I've vomited twice.
presentation.triageNote: 39-year-old female international aid physician who returned from the Democratic Republic of the Congo eight days ago after a torn glove during direct contact with a febrile patient's vomit, now with acute fever, severe myalgia, headache and vomiting.

answer._comment: The authoritative game answer. Explicit ESI, destination, and destination rationale are answer-bearing content; the player's assignment remains session state.
answer.destinationReason: ESI 2 is appropriate because compatible illness within the exposure window after direct body-fluid contact through compromised protective equipment is a high-risk communicable-disease presentation but lacks current lifesaving-intervention criteria.

clinical._comment: Display-ready clinical interpretation derived from patient.presentation. It preserves clinical meaning but must not explicitly name or identify the correct ESI level or destination; it does not participate in scoring.
clinical.summary: This returning aid physician has acute fever, myalgia, headache, and vomiting after a specific high-risk occupational exposure.
clinical.acuityReason: Compatible illness within the exposure window after direct body-fluid contact through compromised protective equipment is a high-risk communicable-disease presentation but lacks current lifesaving-intervention criteria.
expectedResources: Malaria testing and coordinated specialized diagnostics
keyFindings: Returned eight days ago from the DRC
Torn glove during direct vomit contact
Acute fever, myalgia, headache, and vomiting
redFlags: Malaria and other common lethal travel infections remain possible
teachingPoints: Travel alone is not enough. This patient has all three pieces: compatible acute illness, return within the 21-day window and a direct body-fluid exposure through compromised PPE. Isolate first and notify public health, but do not let the Ebola concern delay testing and treatment for malaria or other common lethal infections.
Triage should be based on the current presentation and expected care, with reassessment if new warning signs appear.

possibleClinicalOutcome.disposition: Immediate isolation, public-health coordination, and parallel testing and treatment would lead to specialized admission.

aiImageGeneration._comment: 'aiImageGeneration' is info for AI to generate the image of the patient. Most images were done with openAI gpt-image-1 using an API, not the app, in July 2026. Look for some python scripts that are used to create these images. Be sure that the anchor-image is available and is provided to the AI - otherwise the images will not be consistent.
aiImageGeneration.who: a white 39-year-old female international aid doctor in practical travel clothes, seated on a blue padded clinic chair
aiImageGeneration.pose: slumped forward with elbows near her knees, one hand holding her aching head and a plain travel duffel beside the chair
signs: weak aching posture without any bleeding
aiImageGeneration.prompt: Softly-shaded painterly cartoon illustration in a semi-realistic Pixar/Disney style with smooth gradient shading, soft natural lighting, gentle rounded volumes, fine delicate outlines, warm detailed rendering and natural realistic proportions. Match the attached reference image's painterly style. Full-body wide shot, square 1:1, 3/4 front view, centered. Show the entire person, entire blue padded clinic chair and plain travel duffel with all feet and chair legs and generous margin. Subject: a white 39-year-old female international aid doctor in practical neutral travel clothes with no organization logo. Pose: slumped forward, one hand holding her aching head, travel duffel beside the chair. Expression: feverish, exhausted and seriously ill. Visible signs: flushed sweaty face, heavy tired eyes, weak myalgic posture. Absolutely no blood, bleeding, rash, gore, vomit, PPE costume or sensational imagery. No text, logos, shadows, floor plane, watermark or border. Perfectly flat solid #00ff00 chroma-key background.
